mainEntity.name: How much does Shopify really cost per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Shopify bill has three parts: the subscription (from $29 to over $2,300 a month), the processing fees taken on every order, and the apps you add on top. On a store doing $25,000 a month, processing fees often weigh more than the subscription itself, which is why comparing plans on the sticker price alone is misleading.

mainEntity.name: Which Shopify plan should I pick for my revenue?

acceptedAnswer.text: While your volume stays low, the subscription dominates and Basic wins. As revenue grows, the card rate matters more, and a plan that costs more per month ends up cheaper overall. The calculator gives you the exact switching point for your average order value instead of a generic threshold.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Shopify Payments and an external gateway?

acceptedAnswer.text: With Shopify Payments you only pay your plan's card rate. With an outside provider, Shopify adds a third-party transaction fee of 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, 0.6% on Advanced and 0.2% on Plus, on top of your provider's own rate. At high volume that double commission dwarfs the price gap between two plans.

mainEntity.name: Is the annual Shopify subscription worth it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paying yearly drops Basic from $39 to $29 a month, Grow from $105 to $79 and Advanced from $399 to $299. The saving runs from $120 to $1,200 across twelve months depending on your plan, in exchange for a commitment. The calculator shows the gap for your own numbers when you switch to monthly billing.

mainEntity.name: At what volume should I move to Shopify Plus?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plus almost never pays for itself on price alone when you collect with Shopify Payments: its $2,300 monthly subscription is not recovered through card rates. The trade-off changes with an external gateway, where third-party transaction fees drop to 0.2%. Past several hundred thousand dollars in monthly revenue, that difference can cover the subscription.
